Seminar Title:

Heritage Destination Attributes as Drivers of Brand Equity and Tourist Behavioural Intention: A Visitor-Centric Framework

Seminar Type:

Registration Seminar

Department:

School of Management

Speaker Name:

Khirabdi Tanaya Panda ( Rollno : 524sm2004)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Conference Hall, SM

Date and Time:

25 Sep 2026 12.00pm

Contact:

Rajeev Kumar Panda

Abstract:

Heritage tourism serves as a vital driver of destination development, especially in countries like India, which are endowed with a rich and diverse cultural heritage. UNESCO World Heritage designation provides international recognition and visibility however, such recognition does not automatically translate into a strong destination brand or favourable visitor responses. The manner in which visitors perceive, experience, interpret and emotionally connect with heritage resources plays a critical role in transforming heritage attributes into meaningful destination brand value. Despite growing research on heritage tourism, authenticity, destination image, visitor experience, attachment and destination loyalty these dimensions have largely been examined independently, with limited research integrating them to explain heritage destination brand equity from a visitor perspective. The present study aims to develop and validate a visitor-centric Heritage Destination Branding Framework for selected UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India. The study focuses on the Taj Mahal, Qutb Minar, and Sun Temple at Konark representing diverse cultural and heritage contexts. A mixed-method research design will be employed, beginning with an exploratory phase to identify and refine the key antecedents and dimensions of heritage destination attributes, followed by quantitative testing and empirical validation of the proposed framework. The study will examine the relationships among heritage destination attributes, destination image, destination attachment, heritage destination brand equity and behavioural intention, including the mediating mechanisms through which visitor perceptions and psychological connections contribute to brand value and behavioural outcomes. The framework integrates Customer-Based Brand Equity, Place Attachment Theory to provide a comprehensive explanation of visitor-based heritage brand formation. The study is expected to contribute theoretically by integrating heritage resources, visitor perceptions, psychological connections, destination brand equity, and behavioural outcomes within a unified framework. Practically, it is expected to provide evidence-based insights for tourism authorities, heritage managers and destination management organisations to strengthen destination differentiation, visitor experiences, heritage interpretation and destination brand value.
